    - The oldest room is dry and Wulfric walks past it three times a round. Everything is labelled. Nearly everything.
    - Yes? Be quick, please, and do not move anything; it is all where it should be. I am **Jocelyn**, clerk of the vault.
        - *Choice:* Who are you?
        - *Choice:* What are the ledgers for?
        - *Choice:* Is something bothering you?

    - I found an error in the counting room that three senior clerks had missed. [Aldous](../npcs/aldous.md) came up himself and asked me how many times I count.
    - 'Until it comes out the same twice,' I said. He smiled. He only does that once, so it counted.
    - The vault is its ledgers: what a thing is, whose it is, when it came in, when it may go out. A thing without a label is a thing waiting to be lost.
    - Last winter, at the back of the oldest records room, I found a box. Iron-bound, the vault's old mark on the lid, and in no ledger. None.
    - No key in the vault opens it. [Aldous](../npcs/aldous.md) says it was there before him. So now I look at keys in other people's hands. You would be surprised how many people carry old keys.
